children.text: The same payment screen in English and Arabic, joined across a ruled axis. Motion: rows build on both sides at once, pulses cross the axis row by row, and each tag says what happened: the amount mirrors, the Hijri date reads both ways, the phone stays left to right, the arrow flips.

One Arabic screen annotated like a spec. Motion: the screen builds, then six numbered callouts draw their leaders in turn and type their values, each one a rule Dualkit applies (direction, logical spacing, bidi, Arabic type, Hijri, IBAN).

Six Gulf formats typed the way people type them, with Arabic digits. Motion: a light sweeps the wall diagonally (the measured tile wave), and as it passes each tile its parser runs and the Latin result flips in underneath.
